title: Unification of Egypt
description: Narmer unites Upper and Lower Egypt, launching the dynastic age of Pharaohs.

title: Indus Valley Cities Rise
description: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro flourish into planned cities with drainage, trade, and standardized weights.

title: Akkadian Empire
description: Sargon of Akkad forges a new kind of empire, linking Mesopotamian city-states under one rule.

title: Code of Hammurabi
description: A Babylonian king carves a famous law code into stone, proclaiming order, justice, and harsh penalties.

title: Bronze Age Collapse
description: Palaces burn, trade networks snap, and great powers across the Eastern Mediterranean fall into chaos.

title: Oracle Bones
description: Diviners inscribe questions onto turtle shells and ox scapulae, preserving the earliest known Chinese writing.

title: The Silk Road Opens
description: Han envoys reach into Central Asia, igniting long-distance routes that move silk, horses, ideas, and disease.

title: Thera Eruption
description: A volcanic cataclysm shatters the island of Santorini, sending ash and tsunamis across the Aegean.

title: The Black Death
description: A plague pandemic rips through Eurasia, emptying cities and reshaping economies and empires.

title: Gregorian Calendar
description: A new calendar corrects the drifting year, eventually becoming the global standard for dates.

title: The Scientific Revolution
description: New laws of motion and gravitation crystallize a mechanistic universe, fueling modern science.

title: Germ Theory
description: Invisible microbes are revealed as the agents of infection, transforming medicine, sanitation, and survival.

title: DNA Double Helix
description: The structure of DNA is described, unlocking a molecular blueprint for heredity.

title: Neolithic Age Begins
description: Transition from hunter-gatherer to agricultural societies.

title: Sabretooth Tiger Extinct
description: The Smilodon goes extinct at the very beginning of the Holocene.

title: End of the Last Ice Age
description: Climate warms and glaciers retreat, stabilizing the Holocene epoch.

title: The Awakening of Göbekli Tepe
description: Massive T-shaped pillars carved with predatory beasts are raised.

title: Walls of Jericho
description: Construction of the first stone walls and tower in the Neolithic city of Jericho.

title: Domestication of Cattle
description: Wild aurochs are domesticated into taurine cattle in the Near East.

title: Domestication of Pigs
description: Wild boar are domesticated in the Tigris Basin and China.

title: Growth of Çatalhöyük
description: Large proto-city in Anatolia reaches a peak population of several thousand.

title: Neolithic Expansion
description: Agriculture and the LBK culture begin spreading rapidly across Central Europe.

title: First Irrigation
description: Mesopotamians begin using organized irrigation for crops.

title: Horse Domestication
description: Early taming and milking of horses by the Botai culture in Central Asia.

title: Invention of Glass
description: Core-manufactured glass appears in Mesopotamia.

title: Ötzi the Iceman
description: Life of the famous mummy found naturally preserved in the Alps.

title: Invention of Writing
description: Sumerians in Mesopotamia develop cuneiform.

title: Stonehenge: The First Circle
description: Earth circular bank and ditch formed; Aubrey Holes are dug.

title: Stonehenge Phase 3
description: Bluestones and sarsen stones are arranged into the final familiar patterns.

title: The Great Pyramid of Giza
description: Completion of the massive limestone monolith for Pharaoh Khufu.

title: Stonehenge: The Sarsen Arrival
description: Giant sarsen stones are hoisted into the iconic trilithons.

title: Black Sea Deluge
description: Hypothesized catastrophic flooding of the Black Sea basin.

title: Woolly Mammoth Extinct
description: The last isolated population dies out on Wrangel Island.

title: Tutankhamun Takes the Throne
description: The young Pharaoh begins his brief but famous reign.

title: Burial of Tutankhamun
description: A young king is laid to rest with legendary treasures.

title: Founding of Rome
description: Traditional date for the founding of Rome by Romulus.

title: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
description: Legendary terraced gardens built by Nebuchadnezzar II.

title: Temple of Artemis
description: Completion of the grand temple in Ephesus.

title: Nazca Lines Earliest
description: Ancient geoglyphs are first etched into the desert sands of Peru.

title: Height of Ancient Greece
description: Golden Age of Athens under Pericles; height of Greek cultural influence.

title: Statue of Zeus at Olympia
description: Chryselephantine sculpture of the king of gods is completed.

title: Mausoleum at Halicarnassus
description: Tomb built for Mausolus, satrap of Caria.

title: Colossus and Pharos
description: Rhodes raises a bronze giant; Alexandria builds its lighthouse.

title: Great Wall of China
description: First Emperor unifies the northern walls into a single defense.

title: The Terracotta Army
description: Emperor Qin Shi Huang is buried with thousands of unique soldiers.

title: Rosetta Stone Carved
description: Decree issued in three scripts, later enabling the decipherment of hieroglyphs.

title: Antikythera Mechanism
description: Creation of an ancient Greek analog computer of high complexity.

title: Hero's Steam Engine
description: Description of the Aeolipile, the first known steam engine.

title: Eruption of Vesuvius
description: Volcanic explosion buries the Roman cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

title: Maya Classic Period Peak
description: Zenith of Maya culture, science, and urban construction.

title: Fall of Western Rome
description: Odoacer deposes Romulus Augustulus, marking the end of the Western Empire.

title: Charlemagne's Coronation
description: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans on Christmas Day.

title: Maya Civilization Decline
description: Great cities are abandoned as kings and calendars vanish.

title: Voyage of Leif Erikson
description: Norse explorer establishes a short-lived settlement in North America.

title: Easter Island Moai
description: The first massive stone statues are carved on Rapa Nui.

title: Rongorongo Script
description: System of glyphs developed on Easter Island, potentially an independent invention of writing.

title: Death of Genghis Khan
description: The Mongol Empire reaches its peak expansion under his successors.

title: Invention of Eyeglasses
description: Spectacles for correcting vision are developed in Italy.

title: Gutenberg Printing Press
description: Invention of the movable type printing press.

title: First Sea Circumnavigation
description: The Magellan-Elcano expedition completes the first trip around the world.

title: Copernican Revolution
description: Heliocentric model is published by Nicolas Copernicus.

title: Invention of the Telescope
description: Hans Lippershey applies for the first telescope patent.

title: Great Wall Completion
description: The Ming Dynasty finishes the most extensive version of the defensive wall.

title: Completion of the Taj Mahal
description: Shah Jahan finishes the white marble tomb for his wife.

title: Dodo Bird Extinction
description: The last confirmed sighting of the Dodo on Mauritius.

title: Watt's Steam Engine
description: James Watt patents his efficient steam engine design.

title: Electromagnetic Induction
description: Michael Faraday discovers how to generate electricity.

title: First Automobile
description: Karl Benz patents the Benz Patent-Motorwagen.

title: Antarctic Winter-over
description: The Southern Cross Expedition becomes the first to winter on the Antarctic continent.

title: First Powered Flight
description: Wright Brothers achieve first controlled flight of an aircraft.

title: Amundsen Reaches South Pole
description: Expedition becomes the first to reach the geographic South Pole.

title: First Air Circumnavigation
description: US Army Air Service pilots complete the first flight around the world.

title: Amelia Earhart Disappears
description: Pioneering aviator vanishes during an attempted global flight.

title: The Microchip
description: Invention of the integrated circuit by Jack Kilby.

title: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
description: Humans set foot on the Moon for the first time.

title: World Wide Web Invention
description: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the global hypertext system.

title: ISS First Module
description: Zarya, the first component of the International Space Station, is launched.

title: ISS Completed
description: The International Space Station is declared fully operational.

title: Present Day
description: Today in the Holocene calendar.

title: Ggantija Temples
description: Massive limestone megaliths rise on Malta, built by a culture that then vanishes — older than Stonehenge and the pyramids.

title: Skara Brae
description: A Neolithic village is buried under Scottish sand dunes, its stone furniture preserved intact for five thousand years.

title: Newgrange
description: A passage tomb is built in Ireland, its inner chamber aligned with razor precision to the winter solstice sunrise.

title: Carnac Stones
description: Thousands of standing stones are arranged in long rows across Brittany by a culture that left no explanation.

title: Invention of the Wheel
description: Mesopotamian potters spin the first wheels, and someone realizes they can move things on them.

title: First Sailboat
description: Wind-powered boats appear on the Nile and Persian Gulf, bending nature to move cargo and people across water.

title: Invention of the Plow
description: A simple blade dragged through soil unlocks large-scale agriculture and drives the first population explosions.

title: Varna Gold Necropolis
description: A Bulgarian cemetery yields the oldest worked gold ever found, buried with a single individual of unknown status.

title: Proto-Sinaitic Script
description: Turquoise miners in the Sinai desert scrawl a crude alphabet that becomes the ancestor of nearly every writing system on Earth.

title: First Clay Tokens
description: Mesopotamian accountants track goods with shaped clay pieces, unknowingly laying the groundwork for writing itself.

title: 8.2 Kiloyear Event
description: Glacial meltwater floods the North Atlantic, triggering a cold snap that disrupts early farming cultures across the Near East.

title: Storegga Landslide
description: A colossal underwater collapse off Norway sends a megatsunami crashing across the North Sea, swallowing coastal settlements.

title: Obsidian Trade Networks
description: Anatolian obsidian appears thousands of miles from its source, revealing surprisingly sophisticated long-distance exchange in the early Neolithic.

title: Rise of Carthage
description: Phoenician settlers plant a colony on the North African coast that grows into a maritime empire to rival Rome.

title: Assyrian Empire Peak
description: The world's first true military superpower crushes rivals from Egypt to Persia with iron discipline.

title: Achaemenid Persian Empire
description: Cyrus the Great forges the largest empire yet seen, stretching from the Aegean to the Indus.

title: Gupta Empire Golden Age
description: India's classical peak births decimal numerals, advanced astronomy, and the concept of zero.

title: Tang Dynasty Peak
description: China's most cosmopolitan era opens its capital to the world, blending poetry, silk, and Buddhist art with reach from Korea to Persia.

title: Fall of Constantinople
description: Ottoman cannons breach the walls of the Eastern Roman Empire, ending a thousand-year successor to Rome.

title: Nebra Sky Disk
description: A bronze disk inlaid with gold stars and a crescent moon is buried in Saxony — the oldest known depiction of the cosmos.

title: Voynich Manuscript
description: An illustrated book in an entirely unknown script, filled with unidentified plants and figures, defying decipherment to this day.

title: Dead Sea Scrolls Deposited
description: A sect seals ancient scripture into desert caves at Qumran, where it will lie hidden for two thousand years.

title: Invention of Zero
description: Indian mathematicians formalize zero as a number, laying the foundation for all of modern mathematics and computing.

title: Al-Khwarizmi's Algebra
description: A Baghdad scholar codifies equation-solving into a system, gifting the world both algebra and the word algorithm.

title: First Smallpox Vaccine
description: Jenner inoculates a boy with cowpox and proves immunity to smallpox, launching the age of vaccination.

title: General Relativity
description: Einstein describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime, predicting black holes, gravitational waves, and the expanding universe.

title: Polynesian Settlement of Hawaii
description: Navigators reading stars, swells, and birds sail thousands of miles of open ocean to reach the most remote island chain on Earth.

title: Columbus Reaches the Americas
description: A Genoese captain stumbles into a hemisphere unknown to Europeans, triggering the most consequential collision of civilizations in history.

title: Vasco da Gama Rounds the Cape
description: A Portuguese fleet reaches India by sea, shattering the Arab monopoly on Eastern trade and redrawing global commerce.

title: Samalas Eruption
description: An Indonesian volcano explodes in the largest eruption of the past seven millennia, triggering a decade of famine across Eurasia.

title: Great Fire of London
description: A bakery fire consumes most of the medieval city in four days, prompting a total architectural rebuild and the birth of modern insurance.

title: Assassination at Sarajevo
description: A Bosnian Serb shoots an archduke on a Sarajevo street. The gunshot triggers four years of trench warfare and twenty million dead.

title: Auschwitz
description: Industrial-scale mass murder begins at a converted Polish camp. Six million Jews and millions of others die before the war ends.

title: Hiroshima
description: A single bomb destroys a city. The atomic age begins, and humanity now possesses the means to end itself in an afternoon.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: East Berliners breach the wall to cheering crowds. The Cold War ends without the nuclear exchange both sides had spent forty years preparing.

title: Carrington Event
description: A solar storm overwhelms telegraph wires worldwide; sparks fly from operators' equipment. A storm of that size today would crash the modern grid.

title: Tunguska Event
description: A meteor airbursts over Siberian forest, flattening 2,000 square kilometers of trees. No crater, no impactor recovered, no fatalities — by luck of geography.

title: First Nuclear Chain Reaction
description: Beneath a Chicago squash court, scientists sustain the first controlled nuclear chain reaction. Energy capture at a new order of magnitude — and a new kind of weapon.

title: Sputnik
description: A small radio-emitting sphere reaches orbit, becoming the first human-made object to circle Earth. Humanity has stepped off the planet.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
description: Soviet missiles in Cuba bring the United States and the USSR to within hours of nuclear exchange. Closest documented brush with self-extinction.

title: Voyager Crosses the Heliopause
description: A 1977 spacecraft becomes the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. It carries a golden record of who we were when we sent it.
